text:
nora_ae: FYI - BeaconEdge POC load test is throwing 5xxs during a ramp. They reported short bursts ~100-180 rps. Demo in 20m. Need a quick mitigation and a one-liner we can tell the customer.

sam_support: Which region/model? Any sample request_id or headers from the failed calls?

nora_ae: ap-southeast-1, model=redwood-open-3b-q4-hosted. Example from their harness: 
```
POST /v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-rw-queue-depth: 65
x-rw-backpressure: true
{
  "error": "upstream overloaded, please retry",
  "request_id": "req_be_3321"
}
```
Seeing some 504s too.

pat_runtime: Queue depth ~65 -> autoscaler lag / coldstart problem. Quick, low-risk options: 
1) API-key scoped soft-failover to the 1B variant (no infra spin).
2) temporarily flip allow_burst for the customer so burstpool can attach (needs AE approval).
3) set pool min_replicas=1 for the 3B pool if AE accepts short cost delta.

sam_support: Can we scope failover to only route slow requests so fidelity for normal calls stays high?

pat_runtime: Yes. Command I can run now: 
```
redwoodctl api-keys update --id key-be --set failover_model=redwood-open-1b-q4 --set failover_latency_threshold=600ms
```
That routes requests >600ms to 1B. Zero infra spin.

mike_oncall: If we do min_replicas=1, whats a quick back-of-envelope cost for ap-southeast-1? AE will ask on the call.

pat_runtime: Rough estimate: min_replicas=1 for 3B in ap-southeast ~+$850/day. For a 1-hour demo that's roughly +$35. Failover approach is essentially zero for short spikes. If they want reserved pricing we can give a formal quote later.

sam_support: I can flip the API key failover now if you want. Also grab logs while that rolls: `curl -H \"x-request-id: req_be_3321\" https://logs.internal/bundle` and `redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --since 30m --filter customer=beaconedge`.

nora_ae: Please flip failover and ask BeaconEdge if they want temporary burst enabled. Also need a one-liner to tell the customer about the 5xxs.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3222-01 - \"beaconedge demo ramp - upstream overload\" (link: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-3222-01)

pat_runtime: Flipped failover to redwood-open-1b-q4 with 600ms threshold. Rolling now.

sam_support: Logs + metrics uploaded to the incident. After the failover flip, 502/504 count dropped significantly within ~60-90s. Latency stabilized.

mike_oncall: One-liner for AE to share: \"We temporarily enabled an automated latency-based fallback to a smaller model during brief spikes so the demo remains responsive; full model behavior resumes when load normalizes.\"

nora_ae: BeaconEdge agreed to temporary burst attach if needed. I toggled allow_burst=true.

pat_runtime: Command to enable burst (executed): 
```
redwoodctl customers update --id beaconedge --set allow_burst=true
```
That attached a warm burst replica and eliminated remaining errors.

sam_support: Follow-ups tracked in INC-2026-3222-01: 
- add an AE pre-demo checklist entry: request a 10min prewarm window or enable API failover
- create KB: \"Demo ramp troubleshooting\" with commands and cost bullets
- infra: audit burstpool auto-attach policy (why threshold and policy gating prevented earlier attach)
- perf: evaluate reducing coldstart warmup for top models to <30s

mike_oncall: Also add a quick script for SEs to run locally: token-bucket client example to recommend smoothing the ramp (50rps per 30s).

nora_ae: Demo completed and customer happy. Leaving incident open for infra follow-ups. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
